lead: Islamabad tied itself more visibly to Riyadh's security, with the defence minister pledging 'whatever means' against Houthi attacks as the Saudi crown prince framed the Makkah pact with Pakistan and Türkiye as a pillar of regional stability. At home, Pakistan opened its year chairing the SCO with a rare Indian official in the room, while its feud with Kabul over the Nuristan fighting hardened. On money, the government told IMF reviewers the rupee needs no adjustment even as the Fund pressed for a market-based rate and tighter policy, and new figures put public debt at Rs86.7tr, up 76% in four years.

stories.headline: Indian SCO coordinator in Islamabad as Dar opens chairmanship talks
stories.summary: Deputy PM Ishaq Dar chaired the first SCO national coordinators' meeting of Pakistan's 2026–27 presidency, urging members to turn shared goals into concrete results ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad summit. India's coordinator Alok Dimri attended in person, a rare official visit given the frozen state of bilateral ties.

stories.headline: Pezeshkian defends Pakistan-brokered MoU as US replies to Iran
stories.summary: Iran's president said the Islamabad memorandum had protected Iran's standing while binding Washington to specific commitments, BBC Urdu reported. Tehran separately said it had received a US response to its latest proposal to revive the collapsed Gulf ceasefire, a Reuters report carried by Business Recorder said, keeping Pakistan's mediation track alive.

stories.headline: Pakistan seeks UN, OIC and SCO front on Afghan militancy
stories.summary: Special envoy for Afghanistan Mohammad Sadiq said the lack of an inclusive government in Kabul and the continued presence of militant groups there require coordinated action by the UN, OIC and SCO. The call signals Islamabad's effort to multilateralise its dispute with the Taliban.

stories.headline: Islamabad and Kabul trade blame over Nuristan fighting
stories.summary: Pakistan's information ministry dismissed Taliban accusations of involvement in clashes in Afghanistan's Nuristan province as invented, and repeated its charge that Kabul shelters militant groups. Afghanistan's defence ministry claimed its forces had killed more than 40 militants, including IS members, who it said crossed from Pakistan over three days.

stories.headline: Three militants reported killed in North Waziristan operation
stories.summary: Security forces killed three militants in an intelligence-based operation around Mir Ali, state broadcaster PTV reported citing security sources, who described them as belonging to the group the state calls 'Fitna al Khawarij'.

stories.headline: Asif pledges Pakistan will defend Saudi Arabia against Houthis
stories.summary: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said Pakistan would use whatever means it has to defend Saudi Arabia from the Houthis or any other threat, calling Riyadh's enemies Pakistan's enemies. It is among Islamabad's clearest signals yet that it could be drawn directly into the regional conflict.

stories.headline: Saudi crown prince hails Makkah pact with Pakistan and Türkiye
stories.summary: Opening the Shura Council session, Mohammed bin Salman said the August defence pact, under which an attack on one member counts as an attack on all three, was meant to shore up regional stability. He said recent attacks on Gulf states showed their security could not be separated.

stories.headline: Special forces train with Turkic partners in Uzbekistan
stories.summary: Pakistani special forces joined Türkiye, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan in the Eternal Brotherhood-5 exercise in Uzbekistan from 13 to 25 September, with Kazakhstan observing, state broadcaster PTV reported.

stories.headline: Government tells IMF no rupee or rate change is needed
stories.summary: Officials told the IMF mission the war's economic impact had passed, projecting 7.5% inflation if Brent holds near $80 and a rupee stable around 278 to the dollar, the Express Tribune reported. The Fund urged a market-based exchange rate and tighter monetary policy.

stories.headline: Refiners told to order crude early amid Gulf disruption
stories.summary: Pakistan's largest refiner said the government had instructed refineries to place timely crude orders as shipping through the Gulf faces disruption. The move points to concern over fuel supply security with oil trading above $100 a barrel.

stories.headline: Private firms may get to import LNG directly
stories.summary: The Petroleum Division is weighing wider auctions of unused LNG terminal capacity so power plants and private buyers can import gas themselves, after two terminals sat largely idle since Qatari supplies were disrupted in March. The plan, first reported by Bloomberg, would loosen state-owned Pakistan LNG's hold on spot purchases.

stories.headline: Public debt reaches Rs86.7tr, up 76% in four years
stories.summary: Finance ministry figures show public debt rose from Rs49.3tr in June 2022 to Rs86.7tr by June 2026, of which Rs27.3tr is external. The government plans Rs6.86tr in fresh borrowing in FY27 and aims to shift from short-term bills to longer bonds and sukuk.

stories.headline: Retail investors to trade government debt on the stock exchange
stories.summary: Under an IMF-linked plan to deepen the local-currency bond market, the government said the public will be able to buy and sell treasury bills and bonds through the stock market. The move aims to broaden the investor base beyond banks.

stories.headline: KSE-100 gives back most of early IMF-driven rally
stories.summary: The benchmark index touched 171,493 on hopes for the IMF talks and the bond-market plan, but late selling left it just 369 points higher at 169,969. Analysts cited crude prices near $107 a barrel and the strain on the import bill.

stories.headline: Washington tells Islamabad its Kashmir policy is unchanged
stories.summary: The US has assured Pakistan that it still regards Kashmir as a dispute to be settled between Pakistan and India, Pakistani diplomatic sources told Dawn. Islamabad had protested after the US ambassador to India called Jammu and Kashmir an important part of India during an August visit to Srinagar.

stories.headline: Tarar says India's Indus treaty move sets a global precedent
stories.summary: Launching a report on the suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty at ISSI (govt-linked), Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said Pakistan would not let India use water as a weapon. He argued that Delhi's decision to hold the treaty in abeyance threatens cross-border water governance worldwide.

stories.headline: Centre 'seriously considering' emergency rule in KP
stories.summary: A federal minister said an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was under serious consideration, citing worsening security, as PTI insisted its 4 October march on Islamabad will go ahead.

stories.headline: UN experts call for release of Imaan Mazari and Hadi Chattha
stories.summary: UN rights experts urged Pakistan to free the jailed lawyer couple and drop what they called unfounded charges.

stories.headline: Government defends buying 45 armoured cars for SCO summit
stories.summary: Officials said the bulletproof vehicles are needed to protect leaders at next year's SCO summit in Islamabad, rejecting criticism of the cost.

stories.headline: FBR extends income tax return deadline to 15 October
stories.summary: The tax authority gave filers two more weeks, hours before the 30 September cut-off.
